## Required external generated dependency

Pinned client-go requires `google.golang.org/grpc v1.82.1` and imports its generated `google.golang.org/grpc/channelz/grpc_channelz_v1` client and messages. The canonical schema is checked in as `proto/grpc_channelz.proto` (575 lines, SHA-256 `9931f5b510a5b440717ce2a1890585b4a0dc19b71320df963e04bccfd3c952a7`) and generated by the existing `tikv-client-proto-build` workspace crate into `kvproto/src/generated/grpc.channelz.v1.rs` (1,954 lines, SHA-256 `738311129df74a99f02dbec9653917e88695986a1d934c5345dd566aedf52dfc`). The larger current output includes the repository-wide generated reflection/name implementations added after the original collector receipt. `kvproto/src/generated/mod.rs` exposes the generated client, server, and messages through `grpc::channelz::v1`; `prost-types 0.13` supplies the schema's standard timestamp/duration/any messages.

This is not an approximate schema import. The Go `channelz.pb.go` embedded descriptor at grpc-go tag `v1.82.1` (`ebd8f06a09426fbece97157c95c3917abff28f4e`) and the vendored canonical schema compile to byte-identical 8,373-byte `FileDescriptorProto` payloads, both SHA-256 `65bb440096f199ed4511c92eb0474414d8eeb6f0f30b0fb822f00b092b56b805`.

## Production mapping

| client-go surface | Rust behavior and native decision |
| --- | --- |
| `ChannelzFilter` | `ChannelzFilter` receives a typed borrowed `ChannelzNode::{Channel,Subchannel,Socket}` and returns the exact independent `(collect, walk_children)` decisions. Typed variants replace Go's `any` type switch without changing traversal. |
| `ChannelzCollectorOpts` | Namespace, filter, optional channel trace/state, and independent local/remote socket-label suppression are public in `ChannelzCollectorOptions`; defaults match Go. |
| `NewChannelzCollector` | `new_channelz_collector` accepts an existing Tonic `Channel` to the externally served `grpc.channelz.v1.Channelz` API. `ChannelzCollector::try_new` is the native fallible descriptor-construction companion. |
| Synchronous collection | Prometheus `Collector::collect` blocks until a fresh RPC graph walk completes. Tonic RPCs run on a collector-owned dedicated Tokio runtime and concurrent scrapes use independent client clones/tasks. This is a transport/runtime mapping, not an asynchronous cache: every scrape observes its own live walk, exactly as Go's synchronous `Collect`. The worker terminates and joins when the collector is dropped. |
| Graph traversal | Top channels use source pagination (`start_channel_id`, server-selected page size, max-ID advancement and stop guards). Channel/subchannel/socket nodes have separate seen sets; IDs less than or equal to zero are skipped; cycles and duplicate metrics are suppressed; child channels, subchannels, and sockets preserve source walk/filter/error behavior. |
| Channel metrics | The collector emits exact call counters, last-call timestamp, optional six-state one-hot gauge, optional trace lifetime/creation data, and four severity counts with exact names, help strings, types, and ordered dimensions. Nil data/state/trace/timestamps follow source omission/default behavior. |
| Socket metrics | Streams, messages, keepalives, stream/message timestamps, and local/remote flow-control windows preserve exact counters/gauges and optional address dimensions. IPv4, IPv6, IPv4-mapped IPv6, UDS, other, nil, malformed-IP, and negative-port formatting follows Go `net.IP`/`JoinHostPort` behavior. The all-zero or invalid stream-creation timestamp is omitted while message timestamps retain the source's nil-only check. |
| Fetch failures | `GetTopChannels`, `GetChannel`, `GetSubchannel`, and `GetSocket` failures increment shared wrapping `AtomicU64` counters at the failure site, before that graph walk continues or returns. This preserves client-go's concurrent observability rather than publishing a private per-scrape aggregate only after the entire walk. Child failures do not discard successfully collected parent/sibling samples; a top-level failure terminates only that scrape's walk. The four cumulative error metrics are always emitted. |
| Metric exposition | Up to 13 source descriptors are registered, depending on trace/state options. Every family uses exact namespace/subsystem/suffix/help/type/labels. Manual constant-family construction is the native equivalent of Go's `MustNewConstMetric`; labels are deterministic and counters/gauges retain source values. |

The previously recorded blocker is therefore removed by an explicit transport/runtime implementation: asynchronous Tonic calls are executed on a dedicated collector runtime, while the Prometheus-facing operation remains synchronous, live, uncached, and failure-accounted.

## Test mapping

All six source test declarations are represented one-for-one by independently selectable, source-file-qualified Rust identities:

| Go test | Rust test |
| --- | --- |
| `TestChannelzCollectorCollect` | `source_go_util_collectors_channelz_test_TestChannelzCollectorCollect` |
| `TestChannelzCollectorChannelOptions` | `source_go_util_collectors_channelz_test_TestChannelzCollectorChannelOptions` |
| `TestChannelzCollectorFilter` | `source_go_util_collectors_channelz_test_TestChannelzCollectorFilter` |
| `TestChannelzCollectorSocketLabelToggles` | `source_go_util_collectors_channelz_test_TestChannelzCollectorSocketLabelToggles` |
| `TestChannelzCollectorSkipsZeroStreamTimestamp` | `source_go_util_collectors_channelz_test_TestChannelzCollectorSkipsZeroStreamTimestamp` |
| `TestChannelzCollectorFetchErrors` | `source_go_util_collectors_channelz_test_TestChannelzCollectorFetchErrors` |

The ports preserve the source fixtures as well as their assertions: pagination counters, channel/subchannel states, last-call and trace timestamps, IPv4-mapped addresses, mixed socket address kinds, flow-control windows, filters, optional dimensions, and all partial-fetch errors are exercised over a generated Tonic `ChannelzServer` on a real loopback TCP transport and gathered through a real Prometheus `Registry`. `source_uncovered_address_format_matches_go_for_mapped_and_invalid_ips` covers malformed and mapped address branches. `source_concurrent_fetch_errors_are_visible_before_the_failing_walk_finishes` overlaps two live scrapes and proves the first scrape's child-fetch failure is visible while that scrape remains blocked on a later socket RPC. Before the production fix the second scrape exposed `GetChannel=1`; client-go and corrected Rust expose `GetChannel=2`.

- exact source commit, two-file inventory, line counts, hashes, six-to-six independently named test reconciliation, zero benchmark/example declarations, zero package-local variants/artifacts, zero direct importers, and `git diff --check` passed;
